business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (influenced by Islamic Sharia; unitary national state)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982, entered into force 1986)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) AML/CFT directives; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) UBO disclosure decrees under the economic substance and licensing framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and personal identification documents of each UBO and proposed LLC manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of residence of each individual; subsequently legalized by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Hague Apostille is not accepted by Egypt; documents must be legalized by the Egyptian competent consular authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or competent authority in the corporate shareholder's country of formation; legalized by the Egyptian consular post
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the relevant jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granting authority to the GAFI-accredited local incorporation agent and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the grantor's jurisdiction, countersigned by the Egyptian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization; alternatively, executed before an authorized Egyptian notary for enforcement purposes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory KYC/CDD under AML Law No. 80/2002; all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the CBE/FRA internal blacklists. PEP status is a mandatory data point; enhanced due diligence and beneficial-ownership narrative are required if any shareholder or UBO holds senior public office or foreign political exposure. Continuous monitoring is required for the duration of the commercial relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Services Center / Commercial Registry electronic filing portal (www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed LLC name must be submitted in standard Arabic. A Latin-script transliteration is preserved as a trade name only after GAFI approval, and the Arabic name governs legal identity. Names must not imply public affiliation, religious or military connection, or misleading scope beyond the registered activity. Any foreign-language rendering is subject to the transliteration rules of the Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a GAFI name-rejection decision, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal through the GAFI Companies Registration Directorate within 15 calendar days from notice, attaching three proposed alternative names and the original rejection certificate. The Legal Affairs Committee of GAFI reviews the appeal and issues a decision within 10 working days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate a judicial challenge before the Economic Court within 60 days, with a legal memorandum documenting the non-conflicting, non-misleading character of the requested name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted for a standard Egyptian LLC. The entity must maintain a physical registered office within a recognized commercial building, with a notarized lease agreement, a visible company signboard, and administrative capacity. An IP holding entity must also preserve local substance documentation, including board meeting minutes, books, license registers, and financial records in Egypt.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk, estimated at 35% unannounced on-site inspection in the first financial year, particularly where over 90% of turnover derives from foreign royalty streams and the LLC has no observable local operational footprint. Inspections may be performed by GAFI, CBE, and FRA officials in coordination with the Ministry of Investment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended — chapter governing Limited Liability Companies, and its Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982); read together with the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (establishment and One-Stop Shop procedures) and the Commercial Code No. 17 of 1999 (Commercial Register compulsory registration of merchants and companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Investor Services One-Stop Shop, Commercial Registration Section, Cairo Branch; coordinated with the Commercial Registration Office (Al-Sijil Al-Tegari) at the competent governorate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association (Instrument of Incorporation, Aqd Ta'sis) in the Arabic language, accompanied by the GAFI standard Incorporation Application Form and the Commercial Register introductory application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Egyptian Limited Liability Company; the founders freely fix the capital in the Memorandum of Association and allocate it to subscribed shares. A bank escrow or capital deposit certificate is not a statutory precondition for an LLC, unlike joint-stock companies; cash subscriptions must, however, be paid into the company's corporate bank account within the period fixed by the memorandum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS MEETING of EG LLC, convened in Cairo, Egypt on [date], the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: 1. Share Subscription: The founders irrevocably subscribe to, and the Company accepts, all issued shares as set out in the Subscription Schedule; the managers are authorized to collect subscription proceeds and deposit them into the Company's bank account. 2. Registered Office: The Company's registered office is fixed at [address, Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt] as the official domicile for service of process, statutory notices, and tax correspondence. 3. Officer Appointments: [Name] is appointed General Manager and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each empowered to execute all incorporation, registration, licensing, and banking formalities. Approved unanimously on [date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance – official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; taxpayer e-services portal: https://eservices.eta.gov.eg; national e-invoicing portal: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors establish the Egyptian LLC through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) or the Commercial Registry under the Companies Law (Law 4/2020). The LLC must then register with the ETA using Form TIN-101 through the e-services portal to obtain the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and electronic tax card. VAT registration is effected on the same portal once annual taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000. The taxpayer must also enroll in the national e-invoicing system and obtain X.509 digital-signature credentials. A non-resident licensor of Egyptian-source royalties must obtain an Egyptian withholding tax (WHT) account; registration is processed via the payer as statutory withholding agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the Egyptian-resident LLC is subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income under Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2023. Branches of non-resident entities are taxed under Territorial_Scope on Egyptian-source income only. Pass-through treatment is not recognised. Companies licensed within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) or Investment Law 72/2017 free zones may obtain Tax_Exempt_Zone-modelled treatment under a statutory election, paying an annual 1%–3% duty in lieu of standard income and VAT taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide US-style check-the-box or elective pass-through mechanisms. Available elections include: (i) investment-incentive election under Law 72/2017 (free-zone or special economic zone status), (ii) SCZone regulatory election under Law 83/2015, (iii) voluntary VAT registration election for turnover between EGP 50,000 and EGP 500,000, and (iv) capital-allowance and depreciation elections available to taxpayers. Mandatory anti-avoidance rules — thin capitalisation, controlled-foreign-company and transfer-pricing rules — apply non-elective to IP HoldCo structures; no hybrid-mismatch election is afforded by Egyptian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Value Added Tax under Law 67/2016 and Executive Regulation 66/2017, as amended; ancillary indirect taxes: Customs Duty (Law 207/2020), stamp duty, and real-estate tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 – mandatory VAT registration applies when annual taxable supply turnover exceeds EGP 500,000; voluntary registration is permitted for taxable turnover between EGP 50,000 and EGP 500,000; export-only free-zone activities may register at zero expected turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide e-invoicing (and e-receipts for B2C merchants) under ETA Decree 220/2020, as amended by Decree 180/2021. Taxpayers' ERPs must integrate with the ETA platform using REST APIs and X.509 digital certificates, transmitting XML/JSON invoice payloads for real-time fiscal clearance. Each cleared invoice receives a unique ETA UUID, validation hash and QR digital stamp; invoices not cleared are legally non-compliant and rejected for input VAT recovery on the buyer side. E-receipt integration is phased by turnover, and document rejection generates automated ETA tax audit flags.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (a) exported goods leaving Egypt under a customs export declaration, and (b) export services rendered to a non-resident recipient, benefitting solely outside Egypt, paid in foreign currency from outside Egypt, and supported by an ETA-issued export file. For IP sub-licensing royalties, zero-rating requires the licensed patent/trademark to be exploited wholly outside Egypt, the royalty to be remitted to a bank account in Egypt in convertible foreign currency, and the service to qualify as an exported service under Article 30 of VAT Law 67/2016 and its Executive Regulations; royalties sourced to Egyptian exploitation remain standard-rated and trigger 20% WHT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Egyptian Customs Export Declaration filed through the NAFEZA single window (Customs Law 207/2020)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / international consignment note evidencing physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from a licensed Egyptian bank confirming onshore receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds
Zero-rated VAT export invoice validated with ETA e-invoice QR clearance code
Export or sub-licensing contract, end-user royalty statement and ETA export support file (CEDMS/CARGO-X data match)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA Export Audit Division scrutinises zero-rating claims through full document-matching between customs declarations, e-invoices, bank IRCs and royalty agreements. Failure to repatriate export FX proceeds within 180 days or use of forged documentation results in immediate retrospective clawback of VAT refunds and input credits, a penalty equal to double the evaded tax plus EGP 5,000–50,000 per fraudulent invoice, late-payment interest of 2% per month (capped at 30%), blacklisting from the e-invoicing system, and criminal liability with imprisonment up to five years under VAT Law 67/2016 articles 70–74. Central Bank Law 194/2020 and Anti-Money Laundering Law 80/2002 sanctions may apply cumulatively for foreign-exchange and record-keeping violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the sole currency and exchange-control authority under Banking and Central Bank Law No. 194 of 2020, acting through its Foreign Exchange Committee and the Egyptian Banking Institute clearing systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations for current-account convertibility; royalties and profit remittances are freely convertible at the interbank EGP/USD market rate through licensed banks, subject to documentary controls (license contract, WHT clearance, and CBE purpose codes). The capital account is convertible for direct investment, but each inward equity injection or cross-border shareholder loan requires a dedicated BOP reporting code and bank-level compliance screening. The March 2024 exchange-rate float eliminated the dual-rate regime, clearing the historical FX rationing backlog and reducing remittance settlement to one-to-three business days. Remaining hurdles are documentary: overdue Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) certificates, mismatched five-digit purpose codes, and bank-level risk appetite for IP-holding structures with thin local substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since the 2024 float, the mandatory surrender ratio is zero percent: 100% of export and invisible royalty proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account with a licensed Egyptian bank or converted at the interbank rate. Repatriation is mandatory through the banking system within 90 days from the date of the sub-licensee invoice, extendable to 180 days with bank approval and up to five years for project-based milestone licensing contracts; non-compliance triggers CBE penalties, suspension of the exporter's ETA tax card, and exclusion from FX facilities. Each inbound royalty credit must be linked to the underlying license and an ETA tax invoice, or the bank will reject the purpose-code declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (EGP) / Operational Foreign Currency Royalty Account (USD)
Capital Escrow Account (EGP) / Operational Foreign Currency Collection Account (USD/EUR)
Operational Multi-Currency Account (EGP+USD) with segregated escrow ledger for capital
Operational EGP Disbursement Account / Foreign Currency Fronting Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury rails and MEDIUM for ancillary foreign-currency collection only. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business) are not licensed by the CBE under the Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and applicable CBE fintech regulations; they cannot issue EGP IBANs, cannot clear through CBE RTGS/InstaPay, and are prohibited as the sole account for an Egyptian resident licensor. Receipts routed through an offshore EMI break the 90-day CBE repatriation clock and must be re-invoiced and re-routed through a licensed Egyptian bank to avoid recharacterization as undisclosed offshore proceeds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory for the principal authorized signatory (general manager or board-mandated director) at the selected bank branch for biometric verification and wet-ink signature specimen. Fully remote onboarding is not permitted for non-resident-owned LLCs; at a minimum, consular-notarized board resolutions and powers of attorney are accepted for supplementary signatories, while the principal signatory must appear in person at a branch or before a notary at the Egyptian consulate with a subsequent bank video interview. Required documents: commercial registry extract, tax card, VAT certificate, notarized articles of association, account-opening board resolution, and complete beneficial ownership declarations under AML Law No. 80 of 2002.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP-holdco red flag: same-direction pass-through of royalties from a sub-licensee to an offshore ultimate patent owner with minimal local value added, suggesting round-tripping or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized master license and sub-license agreements with arm's-length royalty rates; Egyptian patent/trademark registration certificates; board minutes evidencing local management substance; transfer-pricing documentation (ETA TP disclosure form, OECD-LP master and local files); audited financial statements with A/R aging and royalty schedules; and an economic-substance opinion from Egyptian counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concern: ultimate beneficial owner resident in a high-risk or high-terrorism-risk jurisdiction, or an ownership chain exceeding three tiers, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and entry visas of all UBOs; complete chain-of-ownership diagram; notarized sources-of-wealth declarations; bank reference letters from the UBO's home bank under correspondent KYC standards; sanctions-screen results dated within 30 days; and an AML compliance memo from the company's designated compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Liquidity disproportionality: projected annual royalty inflows exceeding share capital by more than 50 times without documentary support, indicating a potential conduit or layering structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Five-year cash-flow forecast with signed sub-license pipeline; independent IP valuation report under the income or relief-from-royalty method; audited financial statements of the group; ETA tax returns with CTD credit position; corporate governance chart demonstrating capital adequacy; and a board-approved undertaking to the bank covering expected FX inflows for the first annual cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-route anomaly: sub-licensee requests crediting of royalties to a third-party or consolidation account not named in the license agreement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sources-and-uses settlement matrix; original tax invoices cross-referenced to license receivables; board resolution approving the consolidation account; customer-side legal opinion validating the structure; a negative pledge preventing routing changes without prior bank approval; and Know-Your-Counterparty correspondence with the sub-licensee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: inward equity injection transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank, with field 70 containing '/EQUITY/EG_LLC/' plus the company tax/stamp number and the BOP direct-investment (inward equity) purpose code; the beneficiary Egyptian bank requires the shareholder resolution, commercial-registry extract not older than three months, UBO-KYC on the remitter, and the bank mandate to credit the capital/escrow ledger. Shareholder loans to the LLC must use the BOP foreign-loan purpose code and an executed loan agreement to prevent reclassification as constructive royalties or unlicensed banking activity. Missing or mismatched purpose codes trigger rejection by the CBE electronic clearance gateway, adding three-to-five business days; pre-advice to the receiving branch is therefore mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound upstream royalties: SWIFT MT103 cleared via the bank's correspondent network (typically Fedwire/CHIPS for USD) using BOP services code 277 (charges for use of intellectual property); the bank requires the license agreement, tax invoice, statutory withholding tax settlement certificate (Form 41; 20% domestic rate or treaty-reduced rate) and proof of ETA tax filing (CTD). EGP-denominated operating payments clear through CBE RTGS and InstaPay. For physical-goods trade associated with licensed merchandise, commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) at 30 or 60 days' sight and documentary collections (MT400) are acceptable, supported by the same WHT package and customs invoice to avoid sanctions-screening delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP outright forward contracts, tenor up to 12 months and rollable to 24 months for project-backed exposure, executed under an ISDA 2002 or bank Master FX Agreement, permissible solely against committed royalty inflows evidenced by signed license agreements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/EGP, offered by CBE-licensed dealing banks to hedge expected balances that cannot be physically settled in EGP, settled in USD against the CBE interbank reference rate.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (USD/EGP) with tenors up to five years, permissible where the underlying is a multi-year sub-license franchise with contracted and committed royalty streams.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (CIT form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year (calendar-year filers: by 30 April)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and a 2% per month late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax under Income Tax Law 91/2005; tax card suspension and enforced collection for continued default; no direct administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic substance return (ESR filing for IP and royalty income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Economic Substance Unit, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (annual anniversary filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties of EGP 40,000 to EGP 100,000 for late or non-submission under Law 4/2018 ESR rules; restriction of commercial activities possible; penalties accrue for each year of non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry annual renewal and deposit of audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry; GAFI as registrar for investment-licensed entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the registration anniversary month; financial statements must be deposited within three months of partner approval and no later than six months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-renewal fines and suspension of commercial registration; administrative strike-off after three consecutive years of non-renewal, followed by GAFI de-registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation and AML information update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at commercial registration renewal; within 30 days of any ownership or control change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 50,000 to EGP 100,000 and personal liability of managers for inaccurate UBO declarations under AML Law 80/2002 and its executive regulations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit under Article 95 of Companies Law 159/1981 for limited liability companies whose capital exceeds EGP 250,000 or whose shareholders exceed 10; a global IP patent licensing HoldCo typically exceeds the capital threshold and must be audited annually by an Egyptian licensed auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), materially converged with IFRS; ETA also accepts financial statements prepared under IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Managers must maintain a UBO register and file annual confirmations with the Commercial Registry at renewal; any shareholding transfer requires a within-30-days UBO register update and simultaneous filing before the transfer is opposable to the ETA.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on realized taxable profits for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 (Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 as amended by Law No. 30/2023).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No dedicated IP-box or patent-royalty exemption exists; relevant reliefs include (i) loss carry-forward of 5 years, (ii) Investment Law incentives for eligible activities, (iii) the transitional export-profit incentive under Law 30/2023 (exemption/deduction for repatriated export proceeds, generally for 2023-2025 with phased percentages), (iv) free-zone/SCZone treatment if the IP holding activity is licensed inside a special economic zone, and (v) the ordinary deduction of IP amortization and R&D type expenses; the effective rate for a properly documented licensing entity, after deduction of IP amortization and costs, will therefore typically be lower than the headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 10 (Corporate Income Tax Return) under Law No. 91/2005; filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-services portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg; the form must annex the related-party/transfer-pricing disclosure and the exporter-receipts schedules when treaty relief or export-profit relief is claimed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the ETA may require quarterly provisional payments/advance tax installments for large taxpayers and certain non-resident licensees with a local PE.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 4 months after the end of the fiscal (accounting) year; if the ETA approves an extension, the additional period is in practice limited to 60 days. For a calendar-year EG LLC, the statutory deadline is 30 April of the year following the close of the tax period; final tax payment is due on the same filing date, and monthly delay surcharges accrue thereafter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer registration file number (tight tax card / ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: EG LLC's unique National Taxpayer Registry number and tax file number at the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident licensor with a fixed base/dependent agent in Egypt must first register with the ETA and obtain a tax card before filing; a pure WHT-paying licensor without a PE does not file Form 10 for the royalty income itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Legal form and corporate registry data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form (LLC), commercial registration number, shareholding structure, registered office address, managers and signatures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the branch or the local agent through which Egyptian licensing contracts are made; state the ultimate parent in the TP annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The annual accounting period start and end dates (usually fiscal year ending 31 December).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory accounting period registered with the ETA; the first period must be closed before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Economic activity and ISIC code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal activity: holding, management and cross-border sub-licensing of patents and trademarks, ISIC 6420 (NAICS 533110).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Annotate that the income contains separately scheduled Royalty (20%), dividend (10%), and other Egypt-source income items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross book revenues including royalties, license fees, one-off IP disposals and direct/indirect recovery of IP maintenance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not double-report royalty income already subject to final WHT at 20% if the licensee is the withholding agent; if final WHT was not levied, gross revenues must be declared on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutorily non-taxable revenues (exempt export profits under Law 30/2023 transitional incentive, foreign dividends qualifying for the domestic participation exemption, etc.).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a certificate of export-proceeds repatriation through Egyptian banks if the exemption is claimed for cross-border IP licensing royalty receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs directly attributable to the licensing activity: amortization of acquired intangibles, maintenance and protection costs, technical supervision, sublicense-related legal and WHT costs, and salaries of the Egyptian IP team.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate common headquarters costs via a defensible cost-allocation key and keep supporting transfer-pricing documentation ready.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arithmetic result of Box 5 minus Boxes 6 and 7.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expected to reflect the net arm's length operating margin for the Egyptian PE's IP exploitation function.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowance lines: provisions, unpaid reserves, fines, excess management/technical fees above statutory percentages, unsubstantiated marketing payments, losses from tax-exempt income, and excess interest/royalties under thin-capitalization/TP rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid by the EG LLC to a foreign parent must be supported by an approved license agreement and an OECD-standard TP comparability analysis; a WHT certificate is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Taxable profit after loss carry-forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base after additions and after deducting the available 5-year carried-forward losses (no carry-back).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident with PE may use the Egyptian PE's losses only if tax accounts are maintained in Egypt, carry-forward is continuous, and the ownership-change rules have not terminated the loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headline tax on the Box 10 taxable profit at the statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available to PE taxpayers only; pure non-resident royalty recipients pay the final 20% WHT on gross royalties via the payer's return, not this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Credits (domestic and DTA foreign tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for Egyptian WHT suffered at source and for foreign taxes creditable under a double-tax treaty or the unilateral foreign tax credit rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach original WHT certificates (Shahadat Khasm) and the home-office TRC with apostille for the corresponding calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between Box 11 and Box 12, plus any final quarterly installments already deposited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any underpayment attracts the 2% monthly surcharge and enforcement measures; refunds are only repayable after final assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the legal representative (GM/directors) and the certified public accountant / tax agent, together with annexes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Appoint a resident Egyptian tax agent with power of attorney; the signatory assumes joint civil and criminal liability for the content of the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a delay surcharge of 2% of the assessed tax for each month or part of a month from the statutory deadline through payment; non-filing is punished by an administrative fine of EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 for corporations and is elevated to a 40% concealment penalty where false documentation is submitted; in aggravated evasion, criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment of 3-5 years, bank account freezes and management travel bans.
